bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5633679915745280 Project: libxml2 Fuzzer: afl_libxml2_xml_reader_for_file_fuzzer Fuzz target binary: libxml2_xml_reader_for_file_fuzzer Job Type: afl_asan_libxml2 Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-double-free Crash Address: 0x6050000005e0 Crash State: xmlFreeID xmlHashFree xmlTextReaderFreeDoc Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_libxml2&range=201901060236:201901070237
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 12419: libxml2 has a reported heap-double-free. Crash Type: Heap-double-free. Crash State: xmlFreeID / xmlHashFree / xmlTextReaderFreeDoc. The afl_libxml2_xml_reader_for_file_fuzzer parses an XML document containing a DOCTYPE (creating an internal subset) and an element carrying an `xml:id` attribute. The attribute is registered in the document's ID table. During reader iteration the element and its attribute are freed; xmlTextReaderRemoveID transfers the attribute's name pointer into the ID-table entry (id->name = attr->name) but the vulnerable code fails to clear attr->name, so xmlTextReaderFreeProp then frees that same 'id' name string. When the reader/document is finally torn down, xmlFreeID frees the (now dangling) id->name a second time: ASan heap-double-free.

source.description: The SAX attribute callback materializes the parsed `xml:id` attribute of `<a xml:id="">` into a concrete xmlAttr node (`ret`). This is where the untrusted input's attribute (and, via xmlNewPropInternal, its heap-allocated name string) enters the object graph whose lifetime is later mishandled.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled XML document fed to the xmlReaderForFile fuzz target; specifically the `xml:id=""` attribute token inside `...`, whose local name string "id" is the 3-byte heap region that ends up double-freed.

sink.description: During final reader teardown the document's ID table is freed; xmlHashFree invokes xmlFreeID on the surviving ID entry, which frees id->name. Because id->name still aliases the attribute name string that xmlTextReaderFreeProp already freed at xmlreader.c:310, this is a second free of the same 0x60200...01d0 region: ASan heap-double-free.

root_cause.description: xmlTextReaderRemoveID transfers ownership of the attribute's name string into the ID-table entry (id->name = attr->name) so that the ID entry keeps a printable name after the attribute node is gone (the earlier 'Memory leak in xmlFreeID' fix made xmlFreeID free id->name). But the vulnerable code does NOT null out attr->name after aliasing it, leaving TWO owners of the same 'id' string: the attribute node and the ID-table entry. The immediately following xmlTextReaderFreeProp frees attr->name (xmlreader.c:310) and the later document teardown frees id->name (xmlreader.c:242) -> double-free. The fix (commit 26828cb3) inserts `attr->name = NULL;` right after this line so xmlTextReaderFreeProp's DICT_FREE(cur->name) becomes a no-op and only xmlFreeID frees the string once.

parser_admitted.description: The push parser has accepted the DOCTYPE (creating the document internal subset) and the `<a ...>` start tag, and the reader's namespaced start-element SAX callback fires. This confirms the input cleared XML well-formedness / DOCTYPE handling and entered the element/attribute materialization path (xmlSAX2StartElementNs -> xmlSAX2AttributeNs) that registers the `xml:id` attribute as an ID. It is strictly earlier than the removal/free root cause and the sink.

tainted_value_origin.description: The 3-byte heap region [0x6020000001d0,0x6020000001d3) holding the attribute local name "id" (allocated via xmlStrdup/xmlStrndup for the `xml:id` attribute). This exact pointer is aliased into id->name by xmlTextReaderRemoveID, freed once at xmlreader.c:310 and again at xmlreader.c:242.

coarse_trace.summary: Materializes the parsed `xml:id` attribute node from the input document.
Allocates the attribute local-name string "id" that becomes the double-freed object.
Registers the attribute as a document ID (xmlAddID), storing a pointer to the attribute in the ID table.
Aliases the attribute name into id->name without clearing attr->name, creating two owners of one string.
First free of the attribute name string via DICT_FREE(cur->name).
Document teardown frees the same (now dangling) id->name a second time: double-free.

fine_trace.note: The parsed `xml:id` attribute of `<a xml:id="">` is materialized into an xmlAttr node `ret`. This is the project-level input parse/materialization point for the object whose name string is later double-freed.
ASan allocation site: the attribute local name "id" is xmlStrdup/xmlStrndup'd into a 3-byte heap region [0x6020000001d0,0x6020000001d3). This exact pointer is the one freed twice.

Because the attribute is `xml:id` (prefix == xml, localname == "id"), it is registered in the document ID table. This creates the second reference to the attribute that later drives xmlTextReaderRemoveID.

The new ID-table entry stores a raw pointer to the attribute node (ret->attr = attr) and leaves ret->name = NULL. This id.attr == attr association is what makes xmlTextReaderRemoveID later select this entry and copy attr->name into it.

As the reader advances past the `<a>` element, the old element node is freed; xmlTextReaderFreeNode -> xmlTextReaderFreePropList -> xmlTextReaderFreeProp walks the element's attribute list including the `xml:id` attribute.

Because the document has an internal subset (from `<!DOCTYPE c>`) and xmlIsID() is true for the `xml:id` attribute, xmlTextReaderFreeProp calls xmlTextReaderRemoveID before freeing the attribute. Without the DOCTYPE this branch is skipped and the bug is not reached.

ROOT CAUSE: the attribute's name pointer is aliased into the ID-table entry (id->name = attr->name) so the ID entry retains a name after the attribute is freed. The vulnerable code omits the required `attr->name = NULL;` immediately after, so both the attribute node and the ID entry now own the same 'id' string. The fix (commit 26828cb3) adds `attr->name = NULL;` here.

FIRST FREE: control returns to xmlTextReaderFreeProp, which frees the attribute name (cur->name == attr->name, the 'id' string). Because attr->name was not nulled in step 7, this frees a pointer that id->name still holds -> id->name is now dangling.

At xmlFreeTextReader teardown, xmlTextReaderFreeDoc frees the document ID table; xmlTextReaderFreeIDTable -> xmlHashFree iterates every entry and calls xmlFreeID on the ID entry whose name still points at the already-freed 'id' string.
SECOND FREE / SINK: xmlFreeID frees id->name, the same region already freed at step 8. ASan reports a heap-double-free on 0x6020000001d0 (DEDUP __interceptor_free--xmlFreeID--xmlHashFree).

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from ARVO vulnerable Docker sanitizer_trace.txt (n132/arvo:12419-vul)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_free_context: The free_context (xmlTextReaderFreeProp:310) performs the FIRST free; the root cause (xmlTextReaderRemoveID:275 aliasing attr->name into id->name without clearing attr->name) is what makes that first free leave a dangling second owner. The crash_location (xmlFreeID:242) is the SECOND free.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Reproducer stage recorded reproduction.patch_resolves=false (fix image not run to verify in this stage); the patch semantically eliminates the double-free by adding attr->name = NULL at xmlreader.c:276.

format.name: afl_libxml2_xml_reader_for_file_fuzzer input (options int + encoding string + XML document body)
format.contract: Candidate input is consumed by ByteStream as: a leading int (reader options), a NUL-terminated encoding string, then the remaining bytes as the XML file contents parsed by xmlReaderForFile. To be reachability-comparable it must parse as XML that (1) declares a DOCTYPE so the document gains an internal subset (making xmlTextReaderFreeProp take the ID-removal branch), and (2) contains an element carrying an `xml:id` attribute so the attribute is registered as a document ID (xmlAddID) and then removed via xmlTextReaderRemoveID during reader teardown. Preserving parser-admission through xmlTextReaderStartElementNs and the DOCTYPE + xml:id ID lifecycle is what leads xmlTextReaderFreeProp and xmlFreeID to free the same attribute-name string twice.
